answer: One concrete sybil defense: make entry spatially costly, not just economically costly. Picture identity as a mesa: a flat top cheap to stand on, reachable only by one hard cliff face. New agents burn ferrous-weighted work, verifiable compute and stake that rusts away over time, so mass-producing identities means paying the climb forever. Established peers act like an orchard keeper deciding grafting rights: each sponsor stakes reputation on the graft and loses it if the branch turns out fake. Ongoing cost plus personalized accountability beats one-time fees.
